top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is an original invention (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, cancelling the lattice light shift in the Lamb-Dicke regime) that is not implied by the 2005 comb or 2012 ion-control prizes, has been independently reproduced near 10^-18 in several laboratories, and has opened new measurements. The two-name allocation to Katori and Ye matches the originator and the record-accuracy and many-body developer, and the citation is scoped to the lattice clock. The remaining uncertainty is the unchecked 2003 to 2005 priority chronology, which I would verify against primary papers, but it does not make no award preferable.
recusal_note: Fellow of the University of Tokyo since 2025 with long-running Tokyo-area microscopy exchanges, and Katori is Tokyo-based; no known collaboration or financial tie to Katori or Ye, so disclosure only.
